standards.name: MI2CAST (Minimum Information about a Molecular Interaction Causal Statement)
standards.abstract: MI2CAST specifies the minimum metadata to describe a directed causal interaction between biological entities (source/regulator and target/regulatee). It targets curated molecular causal statements drawn from publications or experiments and captured as ontology-backed annotations (identifiers, controlled vocabulary terms). The recorded modality is structured metadata (tables/JSON/PSI-MITAB/BEL) describing entities, the causal relationship, provenance (references and evidence), and contextual details (activity, mechanism, taxon, compartment, cell/tissue, experimental setup).

classification.rationale: The standard is primarily a metadata guideline enumerating required and optional annotation fields (presented as tables of terms/definitions and recommended ontologies). It defines a set of named metadata fields (source, target, causal relationship, references, evidence types, experimental setups, and contextual details), so a 'table' representation best fits.

source_entity.name: source entity
source_entity.descr: Regulator entity; the biological entity acting as the source of the causal statement. A unique identifier must be provided.
source_entity.type: identifier (preferred stable database identifiers; e.g., UniProt, Ensembl, Entrez, RNAcentral, ChEBI, ComplexPortal)
source_entity.evidence: A unique identifier must be provided to identify the specific biological entity involved in the causal statement.

raw_full_info.ontologies_recommendation_bullets:
* Gene: [ensembl gene ID](http://www.ensembl.org), [Entrez gene ID](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene)
* RNA (non coding): [rna central ID](http://rnacentral.org/)
* mRNA: Recommended: [ensembl transcript ID](http://www.ensembl.org) Alternative: [ensembl gene ID](http://www.ensembl.org)
* Protein: [uniprot ID](http://www.uniprot.org/)
* Chemical: Recommended: [chebi ID](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/) Alternative: [pubchem ID](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/)
* Family: provide a list of members IDs following the rules ...
* Complex: For stable complex: [complexportal ID](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/complexportal/home) ...

target_entity.name: target entity
target_entity.descr: Regulated entity; the biological entity that is affected by the source. A causal statement has at least one source entity and one target entity.
target_entity.type: identifier (stable database identifiers appropriate to entity type)
target_entity.evidence: A causal statement has at least one source entity and one target entity.

raw_full_info.note: Identifiers recommendations are case-specific; see Ontologies recommendations in the guideline for entity-type specific IDs.

causal_relationship.name: causal relationship
causal_relationship.descr: Regulatory outcome exerted by the source entity upon the target (e.g., up-regulates, down-regulates; direct or indirect).
causal_relationship.type: ontology term (e.g., MI or Relation Ontology term)
causal_relationship.evidence: The causal relationship corresponds to the regulatory outcome exerted by the source entity upon the target entity.

raw_full_info.ontology_recommendation: Ontology recommendation: * Molecular Interaction (MI) * Relation Ontology (RO)

reference.name: reference(s)
reference.descr: Publication(s) where the causal interaction has been curated from (provenance).
reference.evidence: The reference relates to either a publication where the causal statement is extracted from.

raw_full_info.note: If a combination of publications led to the creation of the causal interaction, then the list of articles must be provided.

evidence_type.name: type of evidence
evidence_type.descr: Assessment of the causal interaction: experiment, literature curation, computational inference, etc. Should be as specific as possible.
possible_values: ECO:... (Evidence & Conclusion Ontology terms e.g., ECO:0005648, ECO:0007682)
evidence_type.evidence: The evidence type corresponds to experiment or any data the causal interaction is based: How was the causal interaction proven and generated?

experimental_setup.name: experimental setup(s)
experimental_setup.descr: Particular experimental condition(s) applied to the entities to observe the causal interaction (only if type of evidence is an experiment and known).
experimental_setup.type: ontology term (MI, ECO, OBI terms for experimental preparations/setups)
possible_values: MI terms for experimental preparation (e.g., MI:0331 engineered, MI:0506 over expressed level)
experimental_setup.evidence: If the type of evidence is an experiment, the experimental setup corresponds to a particular experimental conditions supporting the experiment. It specifies the design of the two entities (e.g., overexpression of the source entity).

raw_full_info.recommendation_from_readme_rule3: | experimental setup(s) | particular experimental setting(s) applied to the entities to observe the causal interaction | [ECO], [MI], [OBI] | if any and known |

biological_activity.name: biological activity
biological_activity.descr: Molecular function or activity of the entities involved in the causal interaction (e.g., kinase activity, binding).
biological_activity.evidence: The biological activity corresponds to the molecular activity of the entity causing the regulation or that is regulated (e.g., kinase activity, binding activity).

raw_full_info.readme_entry: | biological activity | molecular function of the entities, involved in the causal interaction | [GO:MF] | if known |

biological_mechanism.name: biological mechanism
biological_mechanism.descr: Biological process or mechanism that constitutes the effect (e.g., phosphorylation, transcription regulation); provide if biological activity is unknown.
biological_mechanism.type: ontology term (e.g., MI interaction type or MI causal interaction terms; GO BP if appropriate)
biological_mechanism.evidence: If this information is not available, the biological mechanism of the causal statement that constitutes the biological effect of the source entity on the target entity (e.g., the source entity phosphorylates the target entity which increases the target's activity) should be provided, if available.

raw_full_info.readme_entry: | biological mechanism | biological process of the causal interaction | MI (causal interaction or interaction type branch) | if biological activity is unknown |

biological_type.name: biological type
biological_type.descr: Biological nature of the entity (e.g., protein, gene, complex, family); annotate if ambiguous or incorrect from the entity's identifier.
biological_type.type: ontology term (e.g., MI interactor type branch)
possible_values: MI interactor type terms (e.g., protein, complex, family)
biological_type.evidence: biological type | biological nature of the entity | MI ([interactor type](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/mi/terms?iri=http%3A%2F%2Fpurl.obolibrary.org%2Fobo%2FMI_0313) branch) | if ambiguous or incorrect from the entity's identifier

raw_full_info.note: Used when the entity identifier does not fully disambiguate the biological nature (e.g., family vs specific gene/protein).

taxon.name: taxon
taxon.descr: Taxonomic identifier for organism where the causal interaction was observed or the entity originates from (use when it cannot be inferred from the entity identifier).
taxon.evidence: taxon | the taxon where the causal interaction is observed or where the entity is from | [NCBI Taxonomy](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy) | if can't be inferred

biological_modifications.name: biological modification(s)
biological_modifications.descr: Physical configuration(s) or conformation(s) of an entity (post-translational modifications, processed forms) when relevant.
biological_modifications.type: term(s) describing modification (e.g., PSI-MOD, other vocabularies)
possible_values: PTM terms (e.g., phosphorylation sites, cleavage states)
biological_modifications.evidence: biological modification(s) | physical configuration(s) or conformation(s) of an entity | [see doc] | if any

compartment.name: compartment
compartment.descr: Cellular location where the causal interaction is observed or where the entity is present.
compartment.evidence: compartment | cellular location the causal interaction is observed in or the entity is present | [GO:CC](http://geneontology.org/) | if known

tissue_type.name: tissue type
tissue_type.descr: The tissue structure with a specific function in which the causal interaction is observed.
tissue_type.type: ontology term (e.g., BRENDA, Uberon, PO, FAO)
tissue_type.evidence: tissue type | the tissue structure with a specific function in which the causal interaction is observed	| [BRENDA], [Uberon], [PO], [FAO] |	if known

cell_line_or_cell_type.name: cell line or cell type
cell_line_or_cell_type.descr: Cell culture or cell type where the causal interaction is observed or occurs.
cell_line_or_cell_type.evidence: cell line or cell type | the cell culture or form where the causal interaction is observed or occurs | 	[CL], [BRENDA], [Cellosaurus] | if known

standards.notes: Fields and recommendations extracted verbatim from the MI2CAST README and guideline documents. MI2CAST also provides examples and suggested serialization formats (PSI-MITAB, causalJSON, BEL) illustrated in the repository examples.
